name: Notre Affaire à Tous v France (“Affaire du siècle”, “Case of the Century”)

jurisdiction.court: Tribunal administratif de Paris (Paris Administrative Court)

description: Application by four NGOs (Notre Affaire à Tous, Oxfam France, Greenpeace France, Fondation Nicolas Hulot), supported by more than 2.3 million signatories, against the French State for inadequate climate action and the resulting ecological damage. Article 1246 of the Code civil and the Charte de l'environnement were invoked, with effects also on air quality.
outcome: By the judgment of 3 February 2021 the Paris Administrative Court recognised for the first time the liability of the French State for ecological harm caused by failure to meet emission reduction targets; by that of 14 October 2021 it ordered the State to adopt measures to remedy the surplus of emissions by 31 December 2022. By the judgment of 22 December 2023 the court found that the reparation of the ecological harm was not complete at 31 December 2022, but held that the emission reductions of the first quarter of 2023 covered the remaining part, and therefore dismissed the associations’ requests for enforcement, including the request for a penalty payment. By decision of 13 December 2024 (no. 492030) the Conseil d'État treated the associations’ challenge to that judgment as an appeal and assigned it to the Cour administrative d'appel de Paris (Paris Administrative Court of Appeal).
